text:
anita: FYI nightly SAST found HIGH use of reflection + ObjectInputStream in billing-service (src/main/java/com/redwood/billing/PaymentCodec.java). CI blocked merge.
scanner-bot: [scan] HIGH: insecure deserialization pattern. File: PaymentCodec.java:78-95.
scanner-bot: snippet:
```java
ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(socket.getInputStream());
Object o = ois.readObject();
```
anita: this code decrypts payload with KMS key payment-envelope before deserializing. Need to consider key exposure in triage.
kevin: we have two paths: 1) emergency exception with ephemeral KMS grant and audit evidence, or 2) revert the commit and push minimal patch that replaces deserialization with a safe parser.
lena: ops prefers ephemeral grant for canary if security approves, but require SecOps ticket, RBAC change with condition TTL, and full audit entry.
infra-bot: suggested grant command example: gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/payment/cryptoKeys/payment-envelope --member=serviceAccount:canary-deployer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition='title="sast-emergency-1721112222",expression=timestamp("2026-03-23T12:00:00Z")<timestamp()'
anita: created ticket SEC-2026-211, attaching scan output and repro. Will follow runbook: evidence capture, 1hr grant, canary to 10%, full remediation within 72h or rollback.
kevin: also adding a SAST custom rule to block ObjectInputStream use and a CI premerge check.
lena: thanks, keep updates in the ticket and paste KMS audit id when grant is executed.
